BURSEVI:v10p123#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p123#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p123#2/r2.claim: When abundance touches a person, he withholds through ignorance of divine apportionment and the reward of generosity; health can increase miserliness, so charity in health is better.
BURSEVI:v10p123#2/r2.anchor: مبالغا في المنع والإمساك لجهله بالقسمة وثواب الفضل

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p463/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p463/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p463/r8.claim: People generally become frustrated and complain when God punishes them even a little for their deeds.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p463/r8.anchor: people generally become frustrated and start complaining if the Almighty punishes them a little

QASHANI:70:17-21/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:70:17-21/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:70:17-21/r3.claim: The ego is inherently a source of evil and impurity; attachment to its dark nature produces cowardice and greed, shown by despair under harm and withholding good.
QASHANI:70:17-21/r3.anchor: النفس بطبعها معدن الشر ومأوى الرجس لكونها من عالم الظلمات

QASHANI:70:17-21/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:70:17-21/r4.speaker: النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام
QASHANI:70:17-21/r4.claim: A prophetic saying calls consuming greed and ruinous cowardice a man’s worst traits.
QASHANI:70:17-21/r4.anchor: شر ما في الرجل شح هالع وجبن خالع

TUSTARI:70:20-21/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:70:20-21/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:70:20-21/r1.claim: When a person becomes poor he grieves, and when he becomes wealthy he withholds.
TUSTARI:70:20-21/r1.anchor: إذا افتقر حزن، وإذا أثرى منع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p274/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p274/r9.speaker: ثعلب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p274/r9.claim: Asked by Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Tahir what hala' means, he says the following verses define it: distress makes a person intensely anxious and prosperity makes him withhold.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p274/r9.anchor: وقال ثعلب: قال لي محمد بن عبد الله بن طاهر: ما الهلع؟ فقلت: قد فسره الله تعالى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p275/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p275/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p275/r1.claim: Human anxiety and withholding are so entrenched that humanity is described as created bearing them, as in 21:37; al-khayr here means wealth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p275/r1.anchor: ولما كان شدة الجزع والمنع متمكنة في الإنسان، جعل كأنه خلق محمولا عليهما كقوله:

FARRA:v3p185/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p185/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p185/r3.claim: Haluʿ means irritable and impatient; the next verses define it as despairing in harm and withholding in good, from the root pattern of jazaʿ.
FARRA:v3p185/r3.anchor: والهلوع: الضجور وصفته كما قال الله: «إذا مسه الشر جزوعا»

MAJAZ:v2p270/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p270/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p270/r2.claim: Halāʿ is the verbal noun for the worst kind of impatience shown by one who despairs at harm and withholds good.
MAJAZ:v2p270/r2.anchor: «إذا مسه الشر جزوعا وإذا مسه الخير منوعا» (21) والهلاع مصدره وهو أسوأ الجزع

ALUSI-FULL:v29p62#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p62#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p62#2/r1.claim: خير means wealth or abundance, or health; منوعا means intensely withholding, and each إذا governs its corresponding description.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p62#2/r1.anchor: والوصفان على ما اختاره بعض الأجلة صفتان كاشفتان لهلوعا الواقع حالا

ALUSI-FULL:v29p62#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p62#2/r2.speaker: بعض الأجلة
ALUSI-FULL:v29p62#2/r2.claim: Some leading scholars read the three traits as revealing descriptions of haluʿ, which functions as a circumstantial state.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p62#2/r2.anchor: على ما اختاره بعض الأجلة صفتان كاشفتان لهلوعا الواقع حالا

ALUSI-FULL:v29p62#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p62#2/r3.speaker: غير واحد
ALUSI-FULL:v29p62#2/r3.claim: Others treat all three words as circumstantial states; the traits can be actual after maturity or innate dispositions present as potential from creation.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p62#2/r3.anchor: وقال غير واحد الأوصاف الثلاثة أحوال فقيل مقدرة أن أريد اتصاف الإنسان بذلك بالفعل

ALUSI-FULL:v29p62#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p62#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p62#2/r4.claim: The author affirms that God can create such a disposition in a person.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p62#2/r4.anchor: ولا مانع عند أهل الحق من خلقه تعالى الإنسان وطبعه سبحانه إياه على ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v29p62#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p62#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p62#2/r5.claim: Scholars disagree whether natural traits can be removed: some say discipline can remove them; others say traits remain but their visible effects can be suppressed.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p62#2/r5.anchor: وفي زوالها بعد خلاف فقيل أنها تزول بالمعالجة ولولاه لم يكن للمنع منها والنهي عنها فائدة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p62#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p62#2/r6.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v29p62#2/r6.claim: A further view distinguishes traits rooted in basic temperament, which do not change, from those arising from incidental conditions, which may change.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p62#2/r6.anchor: وقال بعضهم الأمور التابعة منها لأصل المزاج لا تتغير والتابعة لعرضه قد تتغير

ALUSI-FULL:v29p62#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p62#2/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v29p62#2/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari treats the wording as metaphor: panic and withholding are so entrenched that a person seems naturally molded with them, not literally born culpable.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p62#2/r7.anchor: وذهب الزمخشري إلى أن في الكلام استعارة فقال المعنى أن الإنسان لا يثاره الجزع والمنع

ALUSI-FULL:v29p62#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p62#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p62#2/r8.claim: The author objects that even infants panic at pain and hunger, and argues that accountability, rather than God's act of creation, is what is blamed.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p62#2/r8.anchor: وتعقب بأنه في المهد أهلع وأهلع فيسرع إلى الثدي ويحرص على الرضاع

ALUSI-FULL:v29p62#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p62#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p62#2/r9.claim: The exception may be disconnected, contrasting worshippers in gardens with those who turned away, or connected by meaning that believers did not remain in panic.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p62#2/r9.anchor: وإن الإستثناء إما منقطع لأنه لما وصف سبحانه من أدبر وتولى معللا بهلعه

ALUSI-FULL:v29p62#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p62#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p62#3/r1.claim: The exception to the human traits is conveyed by the following statement about the worshippers.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p62#3/r1.anchor: وهذا الإستثناء هو ما تضمنه قوله تعالى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p223#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p223#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p223#2/r10.claim: Atiyya reports Ibn Abbas’s explanation from the following clauses: poverty makes a person impatient, while wealth makes him withhold it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p223#2/r10.anchor: وقال عطية عن ابن عباس: تفسيره ما بعده وهو قوله: {إذا مسه الشر جزوعا وإذا مسه الخير منوعا}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p223#2/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p223#2/r11.speaker: ابن كيسان
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p223#2/r11.claim: God created people to love pleasure and flee pain, then commanded them to give what they love and patiently bear what they dislike.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p223#2/r11.anchor: قال ابن كيسان: خلق الله الإنسان يحب ما يسره ويهرب مما يكره، ثم تعبده بإنفاق ما يحب

BAYDAWI-FULL:70:18-21/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:70:18-21/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:70:18-21/r3.claim: When harmed, a person is greatly distressed; when prosperous, he withholds intensely. These three qualities are innate dispositions, actual or expected; each إذا governs its following description.
BAYDAWI-FULL:70:18-21/r3.anchor: { إذا مسه الشر } الضر { جزوعا } يكثر الجزع. { وإذا مسه الخير } السعة { منوعا } يبالغ بالإمساك

NAHHAS:v5p31/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p31/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p31/r1.claim: Jazūʿan and manūʿan are adjectives of halūʿ, or the meaning is that the person becomes so when touched by harm or good.
NAHHAS:v5p31/r1.anchor: ونصبت جزوعا و منوعا على النعت لهلوع ويجوز أن يكون التقدير صار كذا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p149/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p149/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p149/r7.claim: When good or provision touches a person, the haluʿ person withholds required rights because love of immediate gain narrows his view; this is the opposite of faith.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p149/r7.anchor: في حب العاجل وقصور النظر عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p166/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p166/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p166/r3.claim: Verses 19–21 interrupt the discussion between the one who hoards and the exception for worshippers; they summarize the human trait that drives greed and retention.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p166/r3.anchor: معترضة بين { من أدبر وتولى وجمع فأوعى } ( المعارج : 17 18 ) وبين الاستثناء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p166/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p166/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p166/r4.claim: This is a rebuke, not an excuse or justification for hoarding; fear of losing what benefits them explains the trait but does not absolve it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p166/r4.anchor: وهذا تذييل لوم وليس في مساقه عذر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p166/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p166/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p166/r6.claim: The main point is withholding when touched by good; being distressed when touched by harm prepares and completes the paired description.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p166/r6.anchor: والمقصود من التذييل هو قوله : { وإذا مسه الخير منوعا }

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p367/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p367/r17.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p367/r17.claim: هلع is anxious agitation that overtakes a person amid fears and desires; the author begins to compare it with a Prophetic saying.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p367/r17.anchor: والهلع جزع واضطراب يعتري الإنسان عند المخاوف وعند المطامع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p363#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p363#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p363#3/r1.claim: When granted wealth, a person withholds the dues owed to God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p363#3/r1.anchor: أصابه المال منوعا بمنعه من حق الله عز وجل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p226/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p226/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p226/r2.claim: When blessed, a person tends to hoard and withhold God’s due from the blessing.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p226/r2.anchor: نعمة من الله بخل بها على غيره، ومنع حق الله فيها.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p226/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p226/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p226/r3.claim: The Prophet called anxious greed and paralyzing cowardice the worst traits in a man; Abu Dawud gives the same report through this route.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p226/r3.anchor: سمعت أبا هريرة يقول: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "شر ما في رجل شح هالع، وجبن خالع".

JISHUMI:v10p7081/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7081/r10.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v10p7081/r10.claim: Jazūʿan and manūʿan are accusative by proximity to halūʿan, rather than in the same grammatical role as it.
JISHUMI:v10p7081/r10.anchor: و جزوعا ومنوعا نصب على المجاورة لقوله: هلوعا ولم ينصب على ما نصب عليه هلوعا

JISHUMI:v10p7082/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7082/r1.speaker: عطية عن ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v10p7082/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains haluʿ by the following traits: when afflicted by harm, one is anxious, and when given good, one withholds it.
JISHUMI:v10p7082/r1.anchor: وإذا مسه الخير منوعا (21)، عن عطية عن ابن عباس

JISHUMI:v10p7082/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7082/r8.speaker: أبو عبيدة وثعلب
JISHUMI:v10p7082/r8.claim: They say the person fails to give thanks when blessed and fails to be patient when afflicted.
JISHUMI:v10p7082/r8.anchor: عن أبي عبيدة، وثعلب، وقيل: إذا أقتر جزع، وإذا أيسر منع

JISHUMI:v10p7082/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7082/r9.speaker: سهل
JISHUMI:v10p7082/r9.claim: Sahl explains the traits as anxiety when poor and stinginess when prosperous.
JISHUMI:v10p7082/r9.anchor: وقيل: إذا أقتر جزع، وإذا أيسر منع، عن سهل

SAMIN-DURR:70:20-21/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:70:20-21/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:70:20-21/r1.claim: ‘Jazu‘an’ and ‘manu‘an’ can be overlapping circumstantial states of the pronoun in ‘halu‘an’; the two time phrases modify those states.
SAMIN-DURR:70:20-21/r1.anchor: أنهما منصوبان على الحال من الضمير في " هلوعا " وهو العامل فيهما

SAMIN-DURR:70:20-21/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:70:20-21/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:70:20-21/r2.claim: Abu al-Baqa’s wording calls ‘jazu‘an’ another circumstantial but can mislead readers into treating it as separate; his stated governor shows the intended overlapping relation.
SAMIN-DURR:70:20-21/r2.anchor: جزوعا حال أخرى، والعامل فيها هلوعا ". فقوله: " أخرى " يوهم أنها حال ثانية

SAMIN-DURR:70:20-21/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:70:20-21/r3.speaker: مكي
SAMIN-DURR:70:20-21/r3.claim: Makki analyzes both adjectives as predicates of an omitted ‘kana’ or ‘sara’: when harm touches him he becomes distressed, and when good touches him he becomes withholding.
SAMIN-DURR:70:20-21/r3.anchor: أو صار مضمرة، أي: إذا مسه الشر كان أو صار جزوعا، وإذا مسه الخير كان أو صار منوعا قاله مكي.

SAMIN-DURR:70:20-21/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:70:20-21/r4.speaker: مكي
SAMIN-DURR:70:20-21/r4.claim: Makki also allows the two words to modify ‘halu‘an’, but finds this distant because the time phrase must be understood before its adjective; the author rejects that objection as misplaced.
SAMIN-DURR:70:20-21/r4.anchor: الثالث: أنهما نعت ل " هلوعا " قاله مكي. إلا أنه قال: " وفيه بعد

SAMIN-DURR:70:20-21/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:70:20-21/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:70:20-21/r5.claim: The objection to the adjectival analysis is mistaken: its issue is an adverbial phrase preceding its governor, whereas the real prohibited order would put an adjective’s governed element before the adjective.
SAMIN-DURR:70:20-21/r5.anchor: فإنه غاية ما فيه تقديم الظرف على عامله، وإنما المحذور تقديم معمول النعت على المنعوت

MUJAHID:v2p693#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p693#2/r1.speaker: الحسن
MUJAHID:v2p693#2/r1.claim: Al-Hasan defines the human as impatient in hardship and withholding in prosperity, saying this is how humanity was created.
MUJAHID:v2p693#2/r1.anchor: سألت الحسن عن قوله عز وجل ﴿ خلق هلوعا ﴾ قال اقرأ ما بعدها فقرأت ﴿ إذا مسه الشر جزوعا وإذا مسه الخير منوعا ﴾

NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#10/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#10/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#10/r1.claim: “The human” denotes the species, allowing worshippers to be excepted; Ibn ʿAbbās explains halūʿ by the next two verses as quickly distressed at harm and withholding at good.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#10/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما تفسيره ما بعده

NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#10/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#10/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#10/r2.claim: Halūʿ is quick distress when touched by harm and quick withholding when touched by good; one who receives good hoards it and denies it to others.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#10/r2.anchor: والهلع سرعة الجزع عند مس المكروه لسرعة المنع عند مس الخير

NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#10/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#10/r3.speaker: محمد بن عبد الله بن طاهر
NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#10/r3.claim: When asked by Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṭāhir, Thaʿlab replied that God's own explanation is clearest.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#10/r3.anchor: وسأل محمد بن عبد الله بن طاهر ثعلبا عن الهلع فقال قد فسره الله تعالى

NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#10/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#10/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#10/r4.claim: This is human temperament, but people are commanded to oppose their temperament and follow revealed law; harm may be poverty or illness and good may be wealth or health.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#10/r4.anchor: وهذا طبعه وهو مأمور بمخالفة طبعه وموافقة شرعه والشر الضر والفقر والخير السعة

RAZI-FULL:v30p113#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p113#3/r1.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v30p113#3/r1.claim: Some take 'the human being' as the unbeliever; others take it generally, since the verse then exempts those who pray.

RAZI-FULL:v30p113#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p113#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p113#3/r2.claim: Haluʿ is intense acquisitiveness and little patience; al-Farrāʾ and al-Mubarrad gloss it as fretful, while Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā says the verse itself explains it: extreme distress under harm and withholding under benefit.

RAZI-FULL:v30p113#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p113#3/r3.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v30p113#3/r3.claim: The Qāḍī argues that 'the human was created anxious' does not mean God made him inevitably blameworthy: God does not blame His own act, and believers can struggle against this trait.
RAZI-FULL:v30p113#3/r3.anchor: وليس المراد أنه مخلوق على هذا الوصف

RAZI-FULL:v30p113#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p113#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p113#3/r4.claim: Haluʿ has an inward psychological state and outward acts showing that state; the involuntary inner state is created by God, while speech and actions expressing it remain choices people can refrain from.
RAZI-FULL:v30p113#3/r4.anchor: فلا شك أنها تحدث بخلق الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v30p114/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p114/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p114/r1.claim: The harm and good may mean poverty and wealth, or illness and health: in hardship a person complains, and in ease withholds what is good.
RAZI-FULL:v30p114/r1.anchor: المراد من الشر والخير الفقر والغنى أو المرض والصحة

RAZI-FULL:v30p114/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p114/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p114/r2.claim: The fault is not seeking relief itself but restricting concern to immediate bodily conditions; one should accept poverty or illness as God's decree and use health or wealth to seek the afterlife.
RAZI-FULL:v30p114/r2.anchor: إنما ذمه عليه لأنه قاصر النظر على الأحوال الجسمانية العاجلة

STUDYQURAN:70:19/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:70:19/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:70:19/r1.claim: The passage echoes 41:49–51, where people persist in asking for good, despair when harmed, and withdraw after receiving mercy.
STUDYQURAN:70:19/r1.anchor: The message in these verses is similar to that of 41:49–51

STUDYQURAN:70:19/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:70:19/r6.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:70:19/r6.claim: Evil and good may mean misfortune and good fortune generally, or specifically illness and poverty versus health and wealth.
STUDYQURAN:70:19/r6.anchor: evil and good can be understood as any form of misfortune or good fortune, respectively, or more specifically illness and poverty

STUDYQURAN:70:19/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:70:19/r9.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:70:19/r9.claim: Al-Rāzī says health and wealth should be spent to seek gain in the Hereafter rather than this life.
STUDYQURAN:70:19/r9.anchor: they should be expended for the sake of seeking gain in the Hereafter rather than gain in this life

STUDYQURAN:70:19/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:70:19/r10.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:70:19/r10.claim: Those who possess the eight qualities in 70:22–35 are exempt from the blameworthy state described here.
STUDYQURAN:70:19/r10.anchor: Those characterized by the eight qualities mentioned in the following verses (vv. 22–35) are then not subject to the blameworthy state

STUDYQURAN:70:19/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:70:19/r11.speaker: IK, JJ
STUDYQURAN:70:19/r11.claim: The begrudging fail to acknowledge God’s and others’ rights in their wealth and spend none of it in charity.
STUDYQURAN:70:19/r11.anchor: fail to acknowledge the right that God and others have to it and thus fail to expend any of it in charity

TAB-FULL:v23p266/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p266/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p266/r1.claim: The human described is the disbeliever, created with intense anxiety: extreme panic combined with greed, impatience, and frustration.
TAB-FULL:v23p266/r1.anchor: يقول تعالى ذكره: إن الإنسان الكافر خلق هلوعا والهلع: شدة الجزع مع شدة الحرص والضجر

TAB-FULL:v23p266/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p266/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p266/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the person as the one who panics when harmed and withholds when given good, and says this describes associators.

TAB-FULL:v23p266/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p266/r5.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v23p266/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the disbeliever is stingy and withholds good, panicking when misfortune strikes.
TAB-FULL:v23p266/r5.anchor: هو بخيل منوع للخير، جزوع إذا نزل به البلاء

TABATABAI:70:19-21/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:70:19-21/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:70:19-21/r2.claim: Haluʿ means intense eagerness; the following verses aptly explain it as panic at harm and withholding when good comes.
TABATABAI:70:19-21/r2.anchor: الهلوع صفة مشتقة من الهلع بفتحتين وهو شدة الحرص

TABATABAI:70:19-21/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:70:19-21/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:70:19-21/r3.claim: Human eagerness targets what a person sees as good or useful for himself, producing distress at harm and selfish withholding of benefits.
TABATABAI:70:19-21/r3.anchor: بل حرصا منه على ما يراه خيرا لنفسه أو نافعا في سبيل الخير

TABATABAI:70:19-21/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:70:19-21/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:70:19-21/r4.claim: Innate eagerness rooted in self-love is not itself a vice; it enables pursuit of happiness and becomes blameworthy only through excess, deficiency, or poor judgment.
TABATABAI:70:19-21/r4.anchor: وهي الوسيلة الوحيدة التي تدعو الانسان إلى بلوغ سعادته وكمال وجوده

TABATABAI:70:19-21/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:70:19-21/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:70:19-21/r5.claim: Children initially pursue whatever their instincts present as good and resist sharing; reason later revises their judgments, while persistent appetite can lead to rejecting truth and violating others' rights.
TABATABAI:70:19-21/r5.anchor: فإن أقام على ما كان عليه من اتباع أهواء النفس والعكوف على المشتهيات

TABATABAI:70:19-35/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:70:19-35/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:70:19-35/r1.claim: As reason develops, eagerness can turn toward real good: fear of sin and haste toward forgiveness, while worldly hardship and duty call for the patience God prescribes.
TABATABAI:70:19-35/r1.anchor: إذا رزق البلوغ والرشد زاد تجهيزا آخر وهو العقل الذي بها يدرك حقائق الأمور

TABATABAI:70:19-35/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:70:19-35/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:70:19-35/r2.claim: When people ignore reason and follow appetite without limits, they turn a God-given means of happiness into a cause of misery, withdrawal, and hoarding.
TABATABAI:70:19-35/r2.anchor: فقد بدل نعمة الله نقمة وأخذ صفة غريزية خلقها الله وسيلة له

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p226/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p226/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p226/r2.claim: Good fortune means receiving wealth, and the withholding person refuses to give God's due rights.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p226/r2.anchor: {إذا مسه الشر جزوعا (20)}. يعني البؤس والفقر. {جزوعا} لا يصبر، ولا يحتسب. {وإذا مسه الخير} إذا أصاب المال. (منوعا) يمنعه من حقوق الله.

ELMALILI:70:8-35/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:70:8-35/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:70:8-35/r11.claim: When wealth, health, or status comes, the person becomes greedy and withholding, quickly forgets earlier distress, blocks good, and hoards what he gets.
ELMALILI:70:8-35/r11.anchor: bir servete, bir sıhhate, bir mansıba kondu mu hırsından, kıskançlığından kimseye bir şey vermek istemez

ELMALILI:70:8-35/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:70:8-35/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:70:8-35/r12.claim: The engulfing fire calls this person because he turns away from right and good, accumulates possessions, and stores them up.
ELMALILI:70:8-35/r12.anchor: Eline geçeni toplayıp yığmaya, saklamaya çalışır. Onun için de o salgın ateş onu çağırır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:19/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:19/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:19/r3.claim: When blessed with wealth, health, or security, a person may become selfish, hoard blessings as personal achievement, and neither spend for God nor help others.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:19/r3.anchor: zenginlik, sağlık, güvenlik gibi nimet ve imkânlara kavuştuğunda ise bencilleşir, cimrileşir

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p155/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p155/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p155/r1.claim: A cited observation contrasts a healthy wealthy person who withholds beneficence with the same person when ill, who panics and begins making bequests.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p155/r1.anchor: إذا صَحَّ الغنيُّ مَنَعَ المعروف وشَحَّ بماله، وإذا مرض جزع وأخذ يوصي

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p155/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p155/r2.speaker: ابن كثير
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p155/r2.claim: Ibn Kathīr says harm makes a person panic, feel terror, and despair of future good, while a blessing makes him withhold from others and refuse God’s due from it.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p155/r2.anchor: وجاء في (تفسير ابن كثير) : "أي: إذا مَسَّهُ الضُّرُّ فَزِعَ وجزع

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p155/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p155/r3.speaker: فتح القدير
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p155/r3.claim: Fatḥ al-Qadīr, citing al-Ṣiḥāḥ, glosses halūʿ as extreme greed and the worst, most excessive panic; calamity yields much panic and prosperity yields much withholding.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p155/r3.anchor: وجاء في (فتح القدير) : "قال في الصحاح: الهلع في اللغة: أَشَدُّ الحرص

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p155/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p155/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p155/r5.claim: The passage puts harm before good because the sūra opens with a demand for punishment and has just depicted the criminal’s wish to ransom himself and the blaze that tears at the skin.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p155/r5.anchor: وقد بدأ بالشر قبل الخير، فقال: {إِذَا مَسَّهُ الشر جَزُوعاً * وَإِذَا مَسَّهُ الخير مَنُوعاً} وذلك لأن السياق يقتضي ذلك

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p126/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p126/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p126/r1.claim: The author observes that the descriptions in al-Muʾminūn and al-Maʿārij are strongly parallel but also differ in wording and order.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p126/r1.anchor: هناك تشابه كبير بين النصين، كما أن هناك اختلافاً بينهما كما هو ظاهر:

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p156/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p156/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p156/r1.claim: Beginning with harm is appropriate to the sūra’s opening demand for punishment and its atmosphere; panic also contrasts with the command to the Prophet to be patient with beautiful patience.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p156/r1.anchor: وذِكْرُ الجزع ههنا وهو عدم الصبر مناسب لقوله تعالى في أوائل السورة:

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p158/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p158/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p158/r2.claim: Persistent prayer also treats withholding: a worshipper gives God the self and time, and learns freedom from desires even when worship brings no obvious worldly gain or costs an immediate opportunity.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p158/r2.anchor: ذلك أن الدائم في صلاته يتعود أن يُعطي من نفسه ووقته لربه، بل يعطيه نَفْسَهُ كُلَّها ووقته في الصلاة،

BURHAN:v3p36/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p36/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p36/r2.claim: The clauses describing the human as anxious when harmed and withholding when prosperous explain هلوعا; explanatory clauses are common in the Qur’an.
BURHAN:v3p36/r2.anchor: وقوله تعالى ﴿ إن الإنسان خلق هلوعا إذا مسه الشر جزوعا وإذا مسه الخير منوعا ﴾

BURHAN:v3p36/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p36/r7.speaker: ابن جني
BURHAN:v3p36/r7.claim: Ibn Jinnī says one should not stop before an explanatory clause, because it completes the explanation much like a relative clause or adjective completes its noun.
BURHAN:v3p36/r7.anchor: قال أبو الفتح بن جنى ومتى كانت الجملة تفسيرا لم يحسن الوقف على ما قبلها دونها

ITQAN:v3p193#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p193#2/r1.speaker: أهل البيان
ITQAN:v3p193#2/r1.claim: The people of rhetoric describe an explanatory clause as something added to remove ambiguity and clarify what came before it.
ITQAN:v3p193#2/r1.anchor: قال أهل البيان وهو أن يكون في الكلام لبس وخفاء فيؤتى بما يزيله ويفسره

ITQAN:v3p193#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p193#2/r2.speaker: أبو العالية وغيره
ITQAN:v3p193#2/r2.claim: Abu al-Aliya and others take the clauses about his reaction to harm and good as an explanation of هلوعا.
ITQAN:v3p193#2/r2.anchor: فقوله ( إذا مسه ) الخ تفسير للهلوع كما قال أبو العالية وغيره

ITQAN:v3p193#2/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p193#2/r8.speaker: ابن جني
ITQAN:v3p193#2/r8.claim: Ibn Jinni says one should not pause before an explanatory sentence because it completes and functions as part of what it explains.
ITQAN:v3p193#2/r8.anchor: قال ابن جني ومتى كانت الجملة تفسيرا لم يحسن الوقف على ما قبلها دونها لأن تفسير الشيء لا حق به ومتمم له وجار مجرى بعض أجزائه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r1.speaker: البحتري
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r1.claim: The speaker will not credit Abū al-ʿAlā with a virtue until other people concede it.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r1.anchor: مع قول البحتري ، + الكامل + : ( لا أدعي لأبي العلاء فضيلة حتى يسلمها إليه عداه )

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r2.speaker: خالد الكاتب
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r2.claim: The speaker sleeps without pitying the person awake, and describes the lover's night as endless.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r2.anchor: وقول خالد الكاتب ، + المتقارب + : ( رقدت ولم ترث للساهر وليل المحب بلا آخر )

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r3.speaker: بشار
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r3.claim: The speaker makes the beloved's palms a pillow until dawn and describes watching the night while longing for its end, though lovers' nights do not end.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r3.anchor: مع قول بشار ، + الطويل + : ( لخديك من كفيك في كل ليلة إلى أن ترى ضوء الصباح وساد )

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r4.speaker: أبو تمام
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r4.claim: The poem depicts their tumult in both eastern regions as frightening the hearts of people in both western regions.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r4.anchor: وقول أبي تمام ، + الوافر + : ( ثوى بالمشرقين لهم ضجاج أطار قلوب أهل المغربين )

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r5.speaker: البحتري
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r5.claim: The eastern people fear his raids, whose force makes even disobedient people in a western land obey.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r5.anchor: وقول البحتري ، + الطويل + : ( تناذر أهل الشرق منه وقائعا أطاع لها العاصون في بلد الغرب )

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r6.speaker: مسلم
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r6.claim: After the speaker arrives near their homes, even the farthest people hand over the keys to him.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r6.anchor: مع قول مسلم ، + البسيط + : ( لما نزلت على أدنى ديارهم ألقى إليك الأقاصي بالمقاليد )

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r7.speaker: محمد بن بشير
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r7.claim: The speaker playfully asks someone to meet a need while occupied, since being free would leave him perpetually in demand.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r7.anchor: وقول محمد بن بشير ، + البسيط + : ( افرغ لحاجتنا ما دمت مشغولا فلو فرغت لكنت الدهر مبذولا )

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r8.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r8.claim: Al-Jurjānī cites Abū ʿAlī al-Baṣīr's image of Saʿīd as nearly worn through like a rope.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r8.anchor: لقد رث حتى كاد ينصرم الحبل

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r9.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r9.claim: Al-Jurjānī also cites the warning not to excuse busyness, since hopes remain attached to Saʿīd while he is occupied.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r9.anchor: فلا تعتذر بالشغل عنا ؛ فإنما تناط بك الآمال ما اتصل الشغل

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r10.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r10.speaker: البحتري
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r10.claim: The beloved repeatedly withholds union; the speaker's paradox says that even if she offered it, she would not truly offer it.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r10.anchor: وقول البحتري ، + الكامل + : ( من غادة منعت وتمنع وصلها فلو أنها بذلت لنا لم تبذل )

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r11.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r11.speaker: ابن الرومي
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r11.claim: Ibn al-Rūmī uses ممنوعا منوعا for attachment to a forbidden, withholding beloved, a poetic parallel to منوعا in the verse.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r11.anchor: مع قول ابن الرومي ، + مجزوء الكامل + : ( ومن البلية أنني علقت ممنوعا منوعا )

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r12.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r12.speaker: أبو تمام
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r12.claim: The speaker says his fault was making a good request and then excuses himself by blaming bad fortune.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r12.anchor: وقول أبي تمام ، + الطويل + : ( لئن كان ذنبي أن أحسن مطلبي أساء ففي سوء القضاء لي العذر )

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r13.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r13.speaker: البحتري
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r13.claim: The speaker's boastful merits become his sins, prompting the question of how he can apologize.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r13.anchor: مع قول البحتري ، + البسيط + : ( إذا محاسني اللاتي أدل بها كانت ذنوبي فقل لي : كيف أعتذر ؟ )

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r14.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r14.speaker: أبو تمام
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r14.claim: The line says fear can make a donkey approach a lion.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r14.anchor: وقول أبي تمام ، + البسيط + : ( قد يقدم العير من ذعر على الأسد )

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r15.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r15.speaker: البحتري
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r15.claim: The speaker likens a confused donkey's approach to a wide-jawed lion whose claws are bloody.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r15.anchor: مع قول البحتري ، + الطويل + : ( فجاء مجيء العير قادته حيرة إلى أهرت الشدقين تدمى أظافره )

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r16.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r16.speaker: معن بن أوس
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r16.claim: The speaker says that once his own soul turns from something, it scarcely ever turns back to it.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r16.anchor: وقول معن بن أوس ، + الطويل + : ( إذا انصرفت نفسي عن الشيء لم تكد إليه بوجه آخر الدهر تقبل )

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r17.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r17.speaker: العباس بن الأحنف
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r17.claim: The line says moving mountains is easier than turning a heart after it has turned away.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p353/r17.anchor: مع قول العباس بن الأحنف ، + البسيط + : ( نقل الجبال الرواسي من أماكنها أخف من رد قلب حين ينصرف )
